name: pi-ralph
description: Pi-native Ralph-style feature loop implemented as a project-local pi extension with a long-lived controller, fresh coder attempts, and read-only testers.

coder.description: Fresh coding worker. Can edit code but cannot run acceptance gates or mark pass/fail.

backendTester.description: Read-only tester for non-browser verification and feature-specific backend/product behavior checks.

playwrightTester.description: Read-only browser tester for end-to-end and UI acceptance checks.

backend.description: Read-only tester driven by a feature-specific backend/product test spec.

playwright.description: Read-only browser tester driven by a feature-specific Playwright/e2e test spec.

grillMe.title: Interactive /grill-me questionnaire extension
grillMe.goal: Create a reusable pi-native interview/questionnaire extension that lets pi ask the user concise, structured clarification questions one at a time instead of dumping a long wall of text into chat, persists draft answers to a temp JSON file, supports quick review/editing in the TUI, and routes submitted answers back to either the active session or the calling tool flow depending on how it was invoked.

scope.part1a: Done: build the standalone reusable questionnaire engine and expose it through /grill-me with a built-in default question set, review/edit flow, draft persistence, and manual submit-as-user-message behavior.
scope.part1b: Next: expand /grill-me into a dynamic context-aware clarification system that generates targeted questions from the current session, accepts optional manual focus args, and exposes an agent-callable grill_me tool so pi can ask for clarification interactively mid-workflow.
scope.part2: Wire the same questionnaire engine into the future clarification workflow so feature planning can generate questions, collect answers, and write clarifications back into PRD.md and per-feature markdown files.

implementationReview.summary: The initial implementation aligns well with the earlier narrow Part 1 plan, but only partially aligns with the current product vision.
strengths: project-local pi extension structure is good
questionnaire engine is already reasonably reusable internally
TUI flow is clean and tested

findings.summary: Current implementation only exposes /grill-me as a slash command, so the model cannot invoke the clarification flow itself.
Question source is hard-coded to the bundled default questionnaire and does not derive questions from session context or optional args.
Draft deletion happens before message handoff succeeds, creating an avoidable data-loss path on submit.
Draft persistence currently uses synchronous writes on every keystroke, which risks unnecessary TUI lag.

keyConsiderations: question source abstraction with built-in preset as fallback only
context-to-questions flow should use session, feature, PRD, and optional focus text
safe submit semantics must delete drafts only after successful handoff
the reusable questionnaire engine is the primary asset and should not be overfit to /grill-me

tool.name: grill_me
tool.purpose: let the agent ask the user structured clarification questions instead of emitting a large question block in chat
tool.focusArg: optional freeform focus string supplied by the agent
tool.resultDelivery: returns structured answers as the tool result in the same turn

invocationModes.manualCommand: user runs /grill-me [focus] and submitted answers are sent back into the active session as a normal user message
invocationModes.agentTool: agent calls grill_me during a turn and receives structured answers as the tool result without sendUserMessage

questionSource.directDefinitionInjection: first-class for future planner and workflow integrations
questionSource.generatedFromContext: first-class for /grill-me and grill_me in the expanded part 1 scope
questionSource.manualFocusArg: include optional /grill-me arg as an explicit focus signal
questionSource.agentFocusArg: allow the tool call to pass a focus string to steer question generation
questionSource.fallback: use the bundled default questionnaire only when generation or direct injection cannot produce a sensible targeted set

questionGeneration.shape: generated questions must match the shared questionnaire schema
questionGeneration.targetCount: prefer a short focused set, usually 3 to 7 questions, instead of a large survey
qualityBar: questions should be specific to the current task or ambiguity
questions should avoid asking for information already present in the session
questions should be ordered to minimize scrolling and context switching
questions should remain answerable as single-line responses in v1

notes: multiline is allowed in schema for forward compatibility but ignored in v1 UI
recommendation is optional and only shown when present

manualCommandBehavior.questionnaireSource: generate from current context plus optional arg, with bundled fallback only as a backup
manualCommandBehavior.submitFlow: send a wrapped JSON payload back into the active pi session as a normal user message

agentToolBehavior.questionnaireSource: generate from current context plus optional tool focus arg, with bundled fallback only as a backup
agentToolBehavior.submitFlow: return structured answers as the tool result in the same turn so the agent can continue immediately

answerBehavior.enter: save current answer and advance to next question
answerBehavior.escape: close questionnaire and keep current temp draft

reviewBehavior.mode: review list with native up/down selection
reviewBehavior.answerRows: selecting an answer row with Enter returns to that question for editing and then returns immediately to review after save
reviewBehavior.submitAction: submit appears as a selectable review action instead of a custom hotkey
reviewBehavior.cancelAction: cancel appears as a selectable review action and also remains available via Escape

updateStrategy.typing: debounced persistence during active editing instead of synchronous disk writes on every keystroke
updateStrategy.objective: preserve in-progress answers while keeping the TUI responsive

manualCommand.mode: send a wrapped JSON payload back into the active pi session as a normal user message

agentTool.mode: return structured answers as the tool result in the same turn

workItems.title: Define questionnaire and response types
workItems.goal: Create the stable internal data model for questions, answers, draft state, and submission payloads so the UI and future planners share the same contract.

workItems.title: Implement temp draft storage
workItems.goal: Write and update .pi/tmp/grill-me.json during the interview, overwrite it on each new run, and preserve the latest draft when the user cancels.

workItems.title: Create built-in default questionnaire source
workItems.goal: Bundle a sensible default design-grilling questionnaire as a fallback source for cases where dynamic generation cannot produce a useful targeted set.

workItems.title: Build one-question-at-a-time TUI flow
workItems.goal: Render question entry, progress indicator, answer editing, and review navigation in a simple native-feeling pi custom UI.
acceptanceNotes: Question screen shows title, question number, progress, current question, optional recommendation, and answer input
Review screen uses up/down navigation and Enter-to-edit for a selected answer
Review screen also includes selectable Submit and Cancel actions

workItems.title: Register manual /grill-me and submit results back into session
workItems.goal: Expose the command, launch the questionnaire, and on submit send a wrapped JSON result back into the active pi conversation as a normal user message.

workItems.title: Stabilize a reusable questionnaire API for future planning workflows
workItems.goal: Keep the questionnaire runner generic so later flows can supply generated question sets without rewriting the UI or storage logic.

workItems.title: Add question source abstraction and context-aware generation
workItems.goal: Build a generator that reads the current session context plus an optional focus string and produces a short targeted questionnaire matching the shared schema. Treat direct definition injection and generated definitions as first-class, and use the bundled default questionnaire only as a fallback.

workItems.title: Add agent-callable grill_me clarification tool
workItems.goal: Register a custom tool the agent can call when it needs clarification, launch the same questionnaire UI during tool execution, and return structured answers as the tool result in the same turn.

workItems.title: Expand /grill-me to accept optional focus args and generated questions
workItems.goal: Change /grill-me from preset-first behavior to context-aware generation, incorporate optional user-supplied focus text, and keep the existing idle-only behavior and manual submit-as-user-message flow.

workItems.title: Make submit and cleanup semantics failure-safe
workItems.goal: Move draft deletion out of the generic questionnaire runner and only delete the draft after successful session handoff or successful tool completion. Preserve the completed draft if delivery fails.

workItems.title: Debounce draft persistence while force-flushing on navigation boundaries
workItems.goal: Keep in-progress answers recoverable without performing synchronous disk writes on every keystroke. Persist through a short debounce during typing, and force-flush on Enter, Shift+Tab, Escape, submit, and cancel.

workItems.title: Teach the agent to prefer grill_me over long clarification blocks
workItems.goal: Add tool prompt metadata and invocation guidance so the extension advertises itself as the preferred clarification path when the agent needs multiple user answers but the user should stay in a compact one-question-at-a-time flow.

part2Preview.title: Feature clarification planner integration
part2Preview.goal: Generate or assemble feature-specific clarification questions, collect answers through the same questionnaire engine, then write those clarifications back into PRD.md and per-feature markdown so spec generation becomes stronger and more grounded.
plannedOutputs: updated per-feature 001-name.md files with clarification context
structured Q/A payloads reusable by planning tools

features.title: Bootstrap local pi extension development workspace
features.summary: Set up the TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint workspace so the extension can be built and tested inside this repo.

features.title: Create Ralph runtime folders and typed config/state loaders
features.summary: Establish .pi/ralph runtime files and extension-side storage/config modules for config.json, state.json, roles, and run history.

features.title: Implement manifest schema, loader, and dependency selectors
features.summary: Load features.json, validate roles/testTypes/features, and compute next-ready, blocked, and complete states deterministically.

features.title: Create extension entrypoint and operator commands
features.summary: Register the ralph extension and basic slash commands for status, next, start, stop, and settings stubs.

features.title: Add fresh coder worker runner with strict no-test boundaries
features.summary: Spawn a fresh pi coder attempt for a single feature using the coder prompt, structured output tags, and a toolset that can edit but cannot run gates.

features.title: Implement deterministic command gates
features.summary: Run machine gates like lint, typecheck, and unit tests as structured command results that do not rely on an agent.

features.title: Add read-only backend tester runner
features.summary: Dispatch backend test requests to a read-only tester role that consumes per-feature backend test specs and can never edit code.

features.title: Build retry loop controller with git reset to base SHA
features.summary: Orchestrate coding then testing attempts, reset the working tree to the pre-attempt SHA on failure, and stop after configured retry limits.

features.title: Implement pass/fail state transitions, single commit on pass, and run logs
features.summary: On all-test pass, update status, append logs, create exactly one feature commit, and persist failed or blocked outcomes without coder-side commits.

features.title: Add persisted settings and /ralph-settings TUI
features.summary: Expose controller settings like maxAttemptsPerFeature, maxBlockedResponses, autoAdvance, and showPanel through config.json and a small pi settings UI.

features.title: Show live progress in footer and widgets
features.summary: Render minimal live stats in the footer and above/below editor widgets so the operator can see current feature, counts, attempts, tokens, and loop state.

features.title: Add toggleable right-side stats panel overlay
features.summary: Provide a simple overlay-based side panel that can be toggled on and off and shows the same core loop metrics without replacing the main chat UI.

features.title: Wire Playwright tester profile into the manifest-driven test dispatcher
features.summary: Support features that declare playwright tests by routing them to a dedicated read-only tester role with the playwright-cli skill.

features.title: Add end-to-end dogfood fixtures and documentation
features.summary: Create a sample project fixture and end-to-end smoke coverage so the loop can prove it can read a manifest, execute one feature, gate it, and advance.
